name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (Blackwell), 32 GB
notes: Blackwell consumer flagship: 32 GB GDDR7 on a 512-bit bus, ~1.79 TB/s — roughly 1.8x an RTX 4090's bandwidth, so decode for models that fit is proportionally faster.
Native FP4/FP8 tensor paths (5th-gen Tensor Cores), so NVFP4 checkpoints are architecturally supported here, unlike Ada (RTX 4090). sm_120.
At 575 W TGP it needs a 1000 W-class system; sustained clocks and power headroom are the practical variables between board designs.
32 GB still does not fit a full BF16 27B without offload; it fits larger 4-bit quants than a 24 GB card, which is the reason this class exists.

memory.note: 512-bit GDDR7 at 28 Gbps = 1,792 GB/s; dedicated VRAM, host RAM separate.

compute.note: NVIDIA's GeForce spec page lists 21,760 CUDA cores, 5th-gen Tensor Cores at 3,352 AI TOPS (their FP4-with-sparsity marketing figure), 318 RT TFLOPS, and 2.41 GHz boost. NVIDIA does not publish a clean dense FP32/FP16/FP8 TFLOPS on that page, so those stay null rather than being derived.

thermal.note: 575 W total graphics power; NVIDIA specifies a 1000 W system supply. Founders Edition is 2-slot.

variants.name: GeForce RTX 5090 (Founders Edition)
variants.note: 21760 CUDA cores, CUDA capability 12.0 (sm_120); 2.41 GHz boost
